item.title: 25 years since 9/11, remembrances and a pledge to never forget
item.description: Events to honor the nearly 3,000 who perished on 9/11 and more are underway Friday, including in New York City.

item.description: Around the U.S., ceremonies commemorate the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11th terror attacks in New York and at the Pentagon.

item.title: As diseases loom, CDC's response to measles deaths stirs fears about agency's reliability
item.description: The worst U.S. measles outbreak in decades is growing and flu season is imminent. Experts are fretting about federal health data reliability after the CDC questioned two Pennsylvania measles deaths.

item.title: The voices of Sept. 11: 'My first thought was ... I can't believe that I survived'
item.description: We listen back to interviews recorded in the aftermath of Sept. 11, with a particular focus on stories of survival and loss at the World Trade Center, and some reflections in poetry and music.

item.title: Remembering 9/11. And, Vance, Trump urge voters to back Republicans in the midterms
item.description: NPR reflects on the events of 9/11 and the toll it left on the U.S. 25 years later. And, President Trump and Vice President Vance's convention speeches urge voters to back the GOP in the midterms.

item.title: 25 years later, Americans pause to remember the lives lost on 9/11
item.description: Twenty-five years ago, nearly 3,000 people were killed in the 9/11 attacks. Today, Americans are honoring the lives lost and reflecting on the aftermath of that tragic day.

item.title: They cleaned up ground zero. Now many are hiding from ICE
item.description: After 9/11, thousands of rescue and cleanup crews went to work at ground zero. They were exposed to toxic debris and experienced psychological trauma. Today, many say they live in fear of deportation.
